html:
The Itonama are an Indigenous people of the Amazonian lowlands of northeastern Bolivia, on the Itonamas River and lake in Beni department. Their language was an isolate, related to no other known language; it is now extinct.

In the 1700s Jesuits gathered them into mission towns, as part of the Moxos missions; Magdalena was the main Itonama mission. Their neighbours in the Moxos plains included the Canichana, Movima and Baure, each with a language of their own. Today the Itonama speak Spanish, and their community still lives around Magdalena.
